channel.title: Long Way Round
channel.description: slow stories from Irad, written to be read to the end

item.title: A note before leaving
item.description: I am starting at a newspaper in Talas. A few lines about what these long pages were for. Three years, six long stories, about 4,000 readers. Two of the stories were reprinted in the Talas Herald, one was read on the radio. The projectionist's son came back from Almaty for a week after he read…

item.title: The man at the door of the old bathhouse
item.description: In the Old City of Talas the moncho has stood for two centuries. Its attendant has never taken a bath there. The old bathhouse stands near the Sarchashma Springs, behind a door that is lower than a man. You bow to come in, and Kadyr, the attendant, 64, bows too. He has done it eleven thousand…

item.title: Coal weather
item.description: In Tash-Kömür, the coal town below Iyık Janyl, the first frost is announced by a smell. The men who deliver it say they never have a day off in winter. At six in the morning the town smells of cold iron and smoke, the same smell as a stove that has been lit for the first time in autumn. From the…

item.title: The keeper of Aulie-Ata
item.description: A small town where the Talas leaves its valley, a mausoleum with a green dome, and an old man who has locked and unlocked its door every morning since 1971. Aulie-Ata means holy father. The town is named after the tomb of a ruler of the Kara-Khanids, ten centuries dead, and the tomb is a brick…

item.title: Under the red cliff
item.description: At Kyzyl-Senir, the church's wine ripens in clay jars buried in caves. The brothers who tend it say it is not a winery. It is a patience. The cliff is red sandstone, cut by the river into the shape of a rooster's comb, and all along its foot are black holes: caves, big and small, which people dug…

item.title: Sunday at the sheep market in Bazar-Korgon
item.description: Every Sunday, before sunrise, six thousand animals and a few thousand men arrive in a town at the edge of the Fergana rim. By ten, it is over. The market is a field at the edge of town, behind a wall that nobody has repaired, and it smells like every field in the world on which animals have been…

item.title: The bus to the end of the line
item.description: The village bus runs from the Talas bazaar to the last village before the hills. Two hours, forty stops, and a driver who knows every passenger's mother. The driver, Asylbek, has driven this route for fourteen years. He does not need to look at the passengers; he knows them by their cough. The…

item.title: Forty years of weddings in one lens
item.description: Murat Alibekov photographed the weddings of two generations of Talas. He will tell you which family is still angry about which photo. His studio is a room above a pharmacy, up a staircase with a handrail that wobbles. In the window is a gallery of couples: some in black and white, with the bride…

item.title: Train No. 1
item.description: Seven hours and a quarter from Talas to Nurzhan, in a carriage the age of its conductor, with a samovar that the whole carriage guards. The train leaves at 07:40. At 07:30 the platform fills: women with bags tied in sheets, men with their lunch in a tin, a student with a guitar in a bag, two…

item.title: The museum of the labour collective
item.description: In the antimony-works settlement of Sary-Bulak, the house of culture keeps a museum of the people who built it. Its curator is eighty-one and she knows every face.
